name: Grand Hyatt Tokyo
positioning: Roppongi hotel directly connected to Roppongi Hills, with subtle Japanese aesthetics, mahogany furnishings and suites that include private gardens and a rooftop pool
best_for: Travelers who want a central Roppongi base connected to Roppongi Hills
Guests who want a large suite with a private Japanese garden or outdoor pool
Families who want a suite set up for children

facts.text: The hotel is directly connected to Roppongi Hills, which houses high-end shops and restaurants, a cinema, an art museum and an observatory.
The hotel is a short walk from Roppongi Station and provides easy access to areas such as Ginza and Shibuya.
The design incorporates subtle Japanese aesthetics with rich mahogany furnishings made with natural woods and fabrics.
Rooms feature high ceilings, furniture by B&B Italia and light earth-tone colors and textures.
Rooms have a work desk with Arne Jacobsen's Oxford chair and beds with Egyptian cotton linens by Frette.
Room bathrooms have a deep soaking tub that fills within five minutes.
Suite and club room guests have access to the Grand Club, a private lounge on the 10th floor offering check-in and checkout, a personal concierge, breakfast, evening cocktails and canapes.
Nagomi Spa uses Indigenous elements and open spaces to create a sense of comfort and wellbeing.
A family suite comes with a children's tent, plushies and decorations, and a Japanese-style bathtub.
Wedding venues include the Grand Chapel and a Shinto Shrine ceremony room.
The hotel's restaurants and bars include Japanese, Edo-mae sushi, French bistro and steakhouse options, plus a jazz lounge with live music.
Roku Roku serves Edo-mae-style sushi and sashimi using seafood selected each morning from markets across Japan.

highlights.text: The top-floor suite has a private heated outdoor pool and a sundeck with sweeping views of Tokyo.
A Japanese-style suite has a private Japanese garden, a tatami mat dining room and floor-to-ceiling windows with views of Tokyo.
A corner room on the 21st floor has its own private Japanese garden.
Nagomi Spa and Fitness has a natural red granite indoor swimming pool surrounded by a hardwood deck, and an illuminated whirlpool adorned with platinum tiles made in Italy.
Rooms on the 11th to 20th floors offer views that can include Tokyo Tower, the skyline and Mt. Fuji on a clear day.

considerations.text: Conde Nast Traveler says the entry-level rooms have 20-year-old decor, though they have been well cared for.
Conde Nast Traveler notes that because of the hotel's size, guests may not get the personalized attention of a smaller property.
WhataHotel notes the busy urban location may not suit those seeking tranquility.
